# Meeting the income test

To get Parental Leave Pay, you must meet an income test.

## on this page

- [How the income test works](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/meeting-income-test-for-parental-leave-pay?context=64479#a1)
- [Examples of meeting the income test](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/meeting-income-test-for-parental-leave-pay?context=64479#a2)

We use your adjusted taxable income to work out your eligibility for Parental Leave Pay. If you don’t meet the individual income test, you may meet the family income test.

## How the income test works

We’ll look at your income from the financial year before either:

- the date of birth or adoption
- the date you lodge your claim.

We’ll use whichever date is earlier.

To get Parental Leave Pay, you must have an individual [adjusted taxable income](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/what-adjusted-taxable-income?context=64479) of either:

- $186,487 or less in the 2025-26 financial year
- $180,007 or less in the 2024-25 financial year.

If you don’t meet the individual income test, you can use a family income test. You can get Parental Leave Pay if your and your partner’s [adjusted taxable income](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/what-adjusted-taxable-income?context=64479) is either:

- $386,525 or less in the 2025-26 financial year
- $373,094 or less in the 2024-25 financial year.

Your partner is the person you’re in a relationship with on the date you claim. If you don’t have a partner, your income will apply to the family income test limit.

## Examples of meeting the income test

Expand allCollapse all

Partnered person meeting the family income test

Reema has a baby on 2 July 2026 and lodges a claim for Parental Leave Pay. Her income in the 2025-26 financial year was $215,000. This is over the individual income limit of $186,487.

Reema’s partner Mohammed’s income was $90,000 in the 2025-26 financial year.

Their combined income is $305,000 in the 2025-26 financial year. This is below the family income limit of $386,525. Reema meets the family income test for Parental Leave Pay.

Partnered person meeting the individual income test

Ashley and Dom adopt a child on 9 August 2026.

Dom lodges a claim for Parental Leave Pay. Dom’s income in the 2025-26 financial year was $170,000. Ashley’s income in 2025-26 financial year was $230,000.

Dom is under the individual income limit of $186,487 so meets the income test for Parental Leave Pay. Ashley’s income is over the individual income limit. Dom and Ashley’s combined income of $400,000 is also over the family income limit of $386,525.

Ashley doesn’t meet the individual or family income test for Parental Leave Pay.

Only Dom can get Parental Leave Pay. Because Dom has a partner, he can get a maximum of 110 days of Parental Leave Pay.

Single person meeting the family income test

Indira has a child on 5 August 2026 and lodges a claim for Parental Leave Pay.

Their income in the 2025-26 financial year was $276,000. This is over the individual income limit of $186,487.

We then assess their family income to see if they’re eligible. Indira is single, so is under the family income limit of $386,525.

Indira meets the family income test for Parental Leave Pay.
